title: VII-XI: natural and free will; will of sign and of good pleasure
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): The will belonging toward good pleasure stands as that same by means belonging toward that same which God establishes with Himself a decree concerning things to be done or permitted. XII. The will belonging toward sign stands as that same by means belonging toward that same which God signifies to creatures what He wills to be done by means belonging toward them. XI. SECOND, God's will stands as free. X. Natural stands as that same by means belonging toward that same which God wills according to ye necessity belonging toward His nature. VIII. FIRST, God's will stands as natural or free. VII.
pass_b_english: VII. FIRST, God's will is natural or free. VIII. Natural is that by which God wills according to the necessity of His nature. X. SECOND, God's will is free. XI. The will of sign is that by which God signifies to creatures what He wills to be done by them. XII. The will of good pleasure is that by which God establishes with Himself a decree concerning things to be done or permitted.
source_text: VII. PRIMO enim Dei voluntas est naturalis aut libera. VIII. Naturalis est qua Deus secundum necessitatem naturae suae vult. X. SECUNDO, Dei voluntas libera est. XI. Voluntas signi est qua Deus significat creaturis quid velit ab ipsis fieri. XII. Voluntas beneplaciti est qua Deus apud se decretum constituit de rebus faciendis aut permittendis.
